rationale.conceptual: The paper's method is a custom assembly of established components (FEM, fluid-structure interaction, concrete degradation model, NRBC with wavelet, Newmark integration) that requires a good understanding of structural dynamics and numerical methods. Many interacting equations and physical models must be correctly encoded, going beyond a standard library use.
rationale.execution: The pipeline includes downloading and scaling earthquake records, computing age-dependent concrete properties, building and meshing a 2D FE model with non-reflecting and absorbing boundaries, coupling dam and reservoir equations, running eight linear time-history analyses, and post-processing peaks. It is a multi-stage engineering workflow with heavy implementation demands, though not a huge distributed system.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a multi-component degradation model and a 2D coupled dam-reservoir FEM solver with non-trivial boundary conditions and time-history analysis. The method is non-novel but demands careful translation of many equations and physical principles into code. The pipeline involves several interacting stages and downloading real earthquake records, but remains CPU-only and of moderate computational scale.

compute_estimate.reasoning: A 2D linear FEM analysis of a few thousand DOFs on a small dam-reservoir domain; ground motion records are a few megabytes; no GPU needed; memory estimate is generous for matrix assembly and time integration.
